title: Hedman v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint denied. The sole issue was answered "No": Complainant did not show that Pacific Northwest Presbytery violated the Constitution or clearly erred in adopting five not-guilty judgments on the Leithart charges. The SJC found no procedural violation and left the verdicts undisturbed; it did not annul, remand, or refer, and it urged continued clarification of Leithart's terminology. Separate dissent would have sustained the complaint, found Presbytery erred, annulled the not-guilty verdicts, and directed a new trial or BCO 41 reference.
first_summary: The SJC denied Hedman's complaint, effectively upholding Pacific Northwest Presbytery's not-guilty verdicts on charges that TE Peter Leithart's views conflicted with the Westminster Standards. The SJC deferred to the Presbytery's factual findings because the Complainant failed to show clear error and urged Leithart to clarify his terminology. A dissent would have reversed and remanded.
summary: The SJC denied RE Gerald Hedman's complaint against Pacific Northwest Presbytery, which had adopted five not-guilty judgments on charges that TE Peter Leithart's baptism, covenant, imputation, justification, and union-with-Christ views contradicted the Westminster Standards. Bound to the record and clear-error review, the SJC found no procedural violation and insufficient evidence that Presbytery clearly erred. It left the verdicts undisturbed, declined to endorse Leithart's views generally, and urged continued clarification of his non-standard terminology. A separate dissent would have found error and ordered a new trial or reference.
